name: HubSpot
tagline: A CRM bolted to marketing, sales, service and CMS tooling, sold as one platform.

pricing.basis: per seat, tiered by hub and contact volume
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. HubSpot spans a free tier, cheap Starter seats and Professional plans that cost orders of magnitude more, so a single number would be fiction.

verdictSummary: The part of HubSpot most solo operators actually touch is a contact list, a deal pipeline and a log of what was said and when. That is a weekend build: a table, a kanban board, a notes timeline and CSV import. What does not survive one session is everything that touches the outside world, chiefly two-way inbox sync over Gmail or Microsoft OAuth, sending sequences that land in inboxes instead of spam, hosted forms with tracking, meeting links and the attribution reporting that ties it all together. So you can absolutely replace your use of HubSpot without replacing HubSpot, which is a different claim than beating it.
coreLoopDIY: A local CRM with contacts, companies, a drag-and-drop deal pipeline, an activity and notes timeline per record, tasks with due dates and CSV in and out.
requirements: Node 20 or newer and a local SQLite file
Optional SMTP credentials in .env if you want the app to send plain email
A CSV export from your current CRM to seed the data
whatYouLose: Two-way email and calendar sync, which means logging conversations by hand or not at all
Sequences and deliverability: sending cold email from your own box at scale is a reputation problem, not a code problem
Hosted forms, tracked landing pages and the visitor-to-contact stitching that makes marketing reports mean anything
The integration surface, hundreds of connectors plus everything that already speaks HubSpot natively
Anything resembling multi-user roles, audit trails or a mobile app
moatNotes: HubSpot's real lock-in is that other tools ship HubSpot connectors and your team's habits, reports and workflows are shaped to it. Rip out the CRM and you also rip out ten things quietly writing into it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because HubSpot is not sold as a database, it is sold as the place where marketing, sales and support stop arguing about which spreadsheet is current. For a team, the money buys shared state, an integration that already exists for whatever tool someone bought last quarter, and reporting a non-technical manager can operate. For one person tracking forty deals, most of that is overhead you are paying to avoid, which is exactly why the personal replacement is worth building and the team replacement usually is not.
notes: Build the pipeline, keep the free tier around for whatever needs to receive a webhook.
prompt:
Build a single-user, self-hosted CRM that runs entirely on my machine. No accounts, no cloud services, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/crm.db, schema created on first boot
- Tailwind CSS, plain and dense, no component library
- Server Actions for all mutations, no separate API layer

Data model:
- Company: name, domain, notes
- Contact: name, email, phone, title, company (nullable), tags (comma string), notes
- Deal: title, contact, company, amount, currency, stage, expected close date, probability
- Activity: belongs to a contact or deal, type (note, call, email, meeting), body, timestamp
- Task: title, due date, done flag, optional link to contact or deal

Screens:
1. Contacts: searchable, filterable-by-tag table, row click opens a detail page with editable fields, an activity timeline and a quick "log activity" box
2. Companies: same pattern, plus the list of contacts and open deals attached
3. Pipeline: drag-and-drop kanban over stages (New, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Won, Lost), each card shows title, amount and days in stage, stage changes are written to the activity log automatically
4. Today: overdue and due-today tasks, plus deals with no activity in 14 days
5. Import/Export: CSV import with a column mapping step for contacts and companies, CSV export for every table

Rules:
- Full-text search across contacts, companies and activity bodies using SQLite FTS5
- Optional email send via nodemailer, SMTP config read from .env, feature hidden if the vars are absent. Every sent message is logged as an activity. No sequences, no bulk send, no tracking pixels.
- Include a seed script with about 30 fake contacts and 12 deals so the UI is not empty
- Include a backup script that copies the SQLite file with a timestamp

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: Gmail or Microsoft OAuth inbox sync, hosted forms, landing pages, marketing automation, multi-user auth, roles, permissions, mobile app.

Deliver a README with setup in under five commands and a short list of what this deliberately does not do.
